reference.label: REFERENCE — production engine (three.js r170) in headless Chrome, review JPEG q~0.92 (one JPEG generation)

native.label: NATIVE — talerender (wgpu), clean PNG (no JPEG generation, decision B)

jpeg_floor_note: JPEG floor: the reference frames are JPEG (q~0.92, one generation from the Chrome canvas via Chromium toDataURL image/jpeg 0.93). Measured floor (docs/ab/telemetry/jpeg-decision.md): on flat/step content two otherwise-identical images agree no better than 50.78-57.71 dB; on a detailed frame, one JPEG generation alone measures 42.31 dB against the clean source (mean |d| 1.225, 94.47% of pixels changed, max d 48). A pixel-perfect native frame therefore cannot exceed ~42 dB (detailed) / ~51-58 dB (flat) against these references. The bias is one-directional: JPEG error in the reference is counted as native error, so every number here UNDERSTATES native accuracy; it can never overstate it.
